title: infra check and init exit 2 when something could not be measured -- the code the contract reserves for an unknown or inactive command
body:
FOUND 2026-09-23 by vc while building 0119, whose arm has to account for every command that exits 2.

WHAT HAPPENS. `infra check` exits 2 when something could not be measured (lib/infra.check:331, `rc=2`), and `infra init` exits 2 when a domain could not be read (lib/cmd/infra.d/init:120). The shipped infra page documents both: "2 something could not be measured, which outranks drift", and "`init` exits 2 when a domain could not be read". Eight arms assert them: infra-check.bats:126, 137, 150 and 434; infra-init.bats:188, 217 and 314; infra-profile.bats:331.

WHY IT IS WRONG. usage-rules.md gives 2 to "unknown or inactive", and says "A new refusal takes a NEW code, never a spare one." `bin/devbin infra check` in a project where infra is inactive also exits 2, so a caller cannot tell "infra is not set up here" from "a DNS read failed". This is 0119's defect in a second command, and documentation.bats cannot see it for 0119's reason: 2 is in both sets.

WHO READS THE 2. Nobody, measured. Of 22 repositories under ~/Devel/prj and ~/Devel/cfg, the only infra user outside devbin is Prodinfra. Its README, its TN001 and its geodica profile name no exit code beyond zero against non-zero: "Exit `0` when the estate matches the profile, non-zero when it does not. Safe for cron and CI." (docs/notes/tn0001-estate-target-state.md:270). No workflow or script in any estate invokes infra.

THE FIX. Unmeasured becomes 1, the way a gate that examined nothing is promoted to FAILED rather than given a code of its own. The report still names what was not measured first, so "outranks drift" stays true of the report, though no longer of the code. The page and the eight arms move with it, and 0119's arm then holds every command off 2 with no exception. Ships in 0.1.8 under hv's ruling that everything open goes in the next release; vc builds it with 0121.

## Resolution

Fixed at fbccaa5. Ships in 0.1.8.

- WHAT CHANGED. infra check and infra init exit 1 when something could not be measured, and the report ranks that first. 2 is the dispatcher's code for an unknown or inactive command. Seven arms move from 2 to 1. infra-init.bats:217 stays: it holds an internal yes/no/fault answer, not a process exit. The exit-code headers of lib/infra.check and infra init say 1, and infra.md changes with them.
- THE CONTRACT ARM reads the handlers under lib/cmd for a literal exit or return of 2, and is titled for what it reads. Release's step 6 exits 2 through cut_fail's argument while the arm is green. That is 0130, held for hv's choice.
- RED FIRST AND MUTANTS. Seven arms are red at the base, and the contract arm is red with infra init's or shell-init's 2 restored. X1 (DRIFT printed above COULD NOT MEASURE) is killed. cc's U1-U6 are all killed too.
- REVIEW. cc: approved.
- THE SUITE. The full suite on the series as it landed -- land018 at c130b3a, whose 27 series paths are byte-identical to the landed commits: 1..1653, 1653 ok, 0 not ok, 4 skips (127, 135, 624, 626), rc 0, 12:39:28Z to 13:11:35Z. Each commit passed the gate (guards, critic, doctor) as it landed.
